items.title: Clarence Ford Interview, 1975-12-10
items.q: Emmanuel Gusto, he learned to play clarinet.

ctx.x: Well, was this because most of the music, the pop music?

The music was coming out for saxophone. The clarinet was like a thing of the past, you know. And the guys wanted to, I wanted to saxophone. And if you were just going to play clarinet it would have been more of a Dixieland. I would have had the more of a Dixieland. That's all. And there weren't too many jobs and the Dixieland players, they had many of them. They had too many players for the work, I don't mind. Because every one of them was, George Lewis was working on the riverfront and Willie Humphrey was doing…
What's the band then, you'd have what, two, two tenets? What do you mean, a saxophone? It was a big band.
